thread:
sasha: ran a 4h canary this morning with a phase-aware bucket split (explicit prefill vs decode queues) + conservative fallback policy on rtx-prod pool. sharing quick notes and numbers.

kevin: nice — want the raw profiles or the summary? :eyes:

sasha: summary first. key signals below. full perf traces uploaded to /mnt/perf/runs/2026-03-17/split-batcher-4h.log if you want to dig in.

maria: numbers plz

sasha: p50 decode latency went down ~12ms (28ms -> 16ms). p95 decode also down ~28ms. prefill p50 increased from 42ms -> 57ms (regression). overall token throughput improved 9%.

kevin: interesting. decode wins, prefill loses. any KV-cache churn?

sasha: yes — observed repeated KV cache drains on mid-tail sequences. KV hit rate dropped ~7% during spikes. looks like prefill batches were larger and triggered kernel-selection fallback more often.

maria: kernel fallback? which kernel?

sasha: we saw fallback from our preferred int8 fused-attn kernel -> generic fp16 kernel when sequence length distribution in a prefill batch exceeded the variant's fast-path threshold. fallback counter:+430 in 4h run.

kevin: that explains prefill regression. larger prefill batches pushed mixed-seq batches over threshold, causing scalar fallback. decode batches are smaller/more uniform so stayed on fast kernel.

taylor: can we avoid mixed-seq batches for prefill? maybe bucket by seq_len stricter or lower max_batch_wait for prefill?

sasha: tried stricter bucketization (3 buckets) — reduced fallback count by ~60% but increased queue fragmentation which bumped prefill latency a bit. tradeoff.

maria: what's current queue config?

sasha: pasted config snippet from canary:
```
queues:
  - name: prefill
    max_wait_ms: 8
    token_budget: 80
    bucket_count: 3
  - name: decode
    max_wait_ms: 4
    token_budget: 24
fallback_policy:
  allow_kernel_fallback: true
  kernel_switch_cooldown_ms: 200
```

kevin: token_budget looks low for decode? decode benefited from lower token_budget. prefill needs higher token budget but with stronger bucket windows. maybe token_budget is the wrong knob — we should use max_batch_tokens + seq_len-alignment.

maria: what about KV cache behavior? cache warmup was slow for prefill after low-traffic periods.

sasha: yes, observed cold-starts: first few prefill batches post-idle had KV misses and were slow. after warmup hit rate recovered. propose a tiny warmup traffic spike or keep-alive micro-requests to keep KV hot for critical hosts.

kevin: also instrument kernel selection per-device + per-model variant. add metric: kernel_fallback_count{device,variant,seq_bucket}. that's actionable.

taylor: I'll try two experiments today: 1) increase prefill token_budget -> 110 and reduce max_wait_ms -> 6, keep bucket_count=3, 2) same but with bucket_count=4 and max_wait_ms=5. compare fallback counters and p50/p95.

maria: I'll run a KV-warmup microtraffic on a few hosts for 2h and report.

sasha: one more thing: observed routing fallback to smaller model_variant during capacity spikes which interacts badly with kernel selection. fallback policy allowed variant swap when queue_delay>300ms — that triggered a model change and nuked KV locality. recommend: disallow variant swap during prefill window.

kevin: agree. change request: set variant_swap_threshold_ms to 800 for prefill queue only.

infra-bot: deploy plan queued: split-batcher-tweaks -> canary nodes {rtx-12, rtx-13}. patch id 0x7f3b.

sasha: action items:
- taylor: run 2 canary configs (token_budget+bucket) and push logs to perf path.
- kevin: add kernel_fallback_count metric + per-device labels.
- maria: KV warmup microtraffic on 6 hosts.
- me: disable variant_swap for prefill window and re-run 4h canary.

maria: ack :thumbsup:

taylor: starting experiment 1 now, will paste short summary in this thread in ~45m.

kevin: I'll add metric and Grafana panel for kernel fallbacks.

sasha: thanks all — TL;DR: phase-aware split gives decode win, prefill regressed due to kernel fallbacks and KV cold starts. tuning knobs: bucketization, token_budget, max_wait_ms, variant_swap policy.

kevin: +1, good plan. :rocket:
